chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is obligatory for the Muhrim (one in Ihram) to shave [his head], and if he has already performed Hajj, then if he wishes he may trim [the hair], and if he wishes he may shave [completely]. But if he has tied [the ends of his hair together] or clipped [it], then shaving is obligatory upon him, and trimming is not sufficient for him.

key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: The Muhrim (one in the state of Ihram)
key_terms.عَقَصَهُ: To clip or cut the hair
key_terms.لَبَّدَ: To tie or clump the hair together

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for shaving or trimming hair for a Muhrim who has already performed Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, clarifies the hierarchy of expiation for cutting hair during Ihram, distinguishing between the preferred act of shaving (halq) and the permissible alternative of trimming (taqsir). It establishes that once the hair is styled or clipped in a manner that prevents easy trimming, the pilgrim must revert to the more rigorous obligation of shaving to fully rectify the breach. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on proportionality in kaffarah, ensuring the penalty matches the extent of the alteration to the pilgrim's state.
